text:
I bought a GPU 4 days ago thinking to go for either an RTX 5060 or RX 9060XT coming from an RX 570. I got the 8GB RX 9060XT version because the 16GB is $160 more in my area which is beyond my budget (I'm just a student) - whereas the RTX 5060 was $10 more than the 9060XT 8GB. Knowing that the 9060XT is a class higher than the 5060 and at a much lower price, it was a no brainer to buy it instead.

By that time before actually buying my GPU, I already saw the videos and negative comments about the 8GB version of the 9060XT, but to think that it was cheaper than the RTX 5060, I don't think I purchased the wrong product knowing most stores here still sells the RTX 4060 (yes, 4060) at just $17-$20 less than the 8GB 9060XT and about $30 less than the 5060.

I bought the 8GB 9060XT over the 5060 because:
- the 16GB version of the same card is at least $150-$160 more (USD), as a student, that is a LOT of money
- it has PCIe 5 with x16 lanes compared to only x8 on the 5060 (my PC is PCIe Gen 3)
- close performance to an 8GB RTX 5060Ti which is literally also around $150 more, the same as the 16GB 9060XT
- at least 10-15% more powerful than RTX 5060
- $10 less than the RTX 5060
- I only use a 1080P 120Hz monitor (I really don't see the need for an upgrade, AMD super resolution does the job)

The cheapest 8GB 9060XT here is approx. $380, the RTX 5060 is priced at approx. $390

If you don't turn on the metrics, you literally won't even care about the difference as long as it doesn't dip below 60FPS (for story driven games at least which I play the most), and my 8GB 9060XT runs everything I throw at it above that so I'd say I am happy with my purchase.
